title: Find Minimum and Maximum in Array
statement:
Write a function that takes an array of integers `nums` and returns a two-element array containing the minimum element and the maximum element in `nums` respectively, i.e., `[min, max]`.

The array is guaranteed to contain at least one element.

examples.explanation: The minimum element is 1 and the maximum is 10000.
A single element is both the min and the max.

hints: You can keep track of the minimum and maximum values using two variables.
Initialize `min` and `max` to the first element of the array, then iterate through the rest of the array.
For each element, check if it is smaller than `min` (and update `min` if so) or larger than `max` (and update `max` if so).

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Sort the array in non-decreasing order. The first element will be the minimum and the last element will be the maximum.

optimizedSolution.explanation: Iterate through the array once. Maintain two variables `min` and `max` initialized to the first element. Update them if any smaller or larger element is encountered.

interviewExplanation: The brute-force method sorts the array, which takes O(n log n) time. We optimize it to O(n) by performing a single scan of the array, updating our min and max values on-the-fly, requiring only O(1) auxiliary space.

editorial.approach: A single linear scan through the array of size `n` initialized with `min = nums[0]` and `max = nums[0]` gives the optimal time complexity of O(n) with O(1) space.
